subject: PrivDeploy: order form redlines + evidence matrix and timeline
messages:
From: Monica Ruiz <monica.ruiz@novushealth.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Peter Klein <p.klein@novushealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on on-prem addendum + evidence timeline

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. The team liked the isolation/kv cache controls you showed. Legal has one pass through the draft MSA + Order Form and flagged two areas we need clarified before we can start procurement:

1) License boundary language in the Private Deployment Addendum — they want explicit wording about operator-run consoles and whether snapshots transferred for audit count as a "deliverable" under the license (we currently have a concern about residency).
2) Evidence delivery cadence — need a concrete timeline for when operator capability evidence (runbook, witness test, snapshot proof) will be provided and whether those artifacts are covered under your standard data retention terms.

I've attached our internal list of asks but wanted to get your suggested approach as we aim to get an exec sign in ~2 weeks. Can Redwood provide: a short evidence matrix (what you'll deliver, format, and expected delivery date) and a proposed sentence for the license scope that prevents marketable redistribution but allows customer-run forensic snapshots for audit?

Best,
Monica
--
Monica Ruiz
Head of Procurement, Novus Health AI
monica.ruiz@novushealth.ai
+1 415-555-0134

-----Original attachment: EvidenceMatrix_Novus_20270429.xlsx (xlsx)

---
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Ruiz <monica.ruiz@novushealth.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on on-prem addendum + evidence timeline

Monica — thanks, and appreciate the clear list. Looping in Lauren (legal lead on PrivDeploy addenda) and Naomi (solutions lead) to propose language and a delivery plan. High level:

- License scope: we can add a carve that allows the customer to make and retain forensic snapshots strictly for internal audit/compliance; snapshots remain the customer’s copy and are not redistributable. Redwood retains the right to define minimal runtime artifacts we need to provide support (logs/diagnostics) but we will exclude any language that would enable Novus to publish or redistribute our model weights or runtime binaries.

- Evidence matrix: Naomi will propose a 3-step delivery (initial runbook + operator checklist; witnessed test session; evidence bundle with snapshot hash and decryption attestation) — target delivery across a two-week window post-execution of SOW/order form.

Action items: Lauren — can you review and draft a concise addendum sentence and confirm whether we need any internal approvals for the wording around snapshots as "customer-owned copies"? Naomi — can you attach the proposed matrix and tentative dates. Monica — will this timeline work against your procurement window?

Best,
David

--
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Ruiz <monica.ruiz@novushealth.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on on-prem addendum + evidence timeline

Monica, David — quick legal note after internal review. Draft proposed language below; happy to iterate.

Proposed license carve (single sentence to add to Private Deployment Addendum):
"Customer may create and retain environment snapshots and associated forensic artifacts solely for internal audit and compliance purposes; such artifacts shall remain Customer-owned and shall not be reproduced, distributed, or used to create derivative models, and shall not constitute a transfer of Redwood's model weights, binaries, or proprietary runtime components."

Notes:
- This keeps a clear ownership boundary while enabling the customer to keep evidence for audits.
- We recommend adding a short definition for "forensic artifacts" in the exhibit (e.g., snapshot hash, operator runbook, witness session recording) to avoid later ambiguity.
- If Novus requires an escrow-style custody for keys or operator credentials, we treat that as a separate commercial request and will escalate to PM/sales for pricing and SLA carveouts.

I'll mark the proposed sentence as tracked changes in the MSA redline and circulate once Naomi provides the exhibit definition.

Thanks,
Lauren

--
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Ruiz <monica.ruiz@novushealth.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on on-prem addendum + evidence timeline

Monica — attached is the evidence matrix and a proposed delivery schedule. Summary here:

1) Day 0-3: Delivery of Runbook and Operator Checklist (PDF) + index of artifacts.
2) Day 4-7: Witnessed acceptance test (30-60 min remote session) where Redwood demonstrates snapshot creation and provides a signed hash.
3) Day 8-14: Evidence bundle delivered (snapshot metadata, hash, decryption attestation if applicable, and a short witness test recording).

We treat operator credentials and key-handback as a separate optional pathway; if Novus wants Redwood to custody encryption keys or a sealed-handback through a third-party escrow, that needs scope/pricing. The Excel has fields for format (pdf/zip/mp4), retention recommendations (90 days default for witness assets), and handoff owners.

Attachment: EvidenceMatrix_Novus_20270430.xlsx (xlsx)

Let me know if you want me to push the witness window earlier — we can run a test session the week of May 3 if you sign the Order Form by EOD May 1.

Naomi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

--
From: Peter Klein <p.klein@novushealth.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Ruiz <monica.ruiz@novushealth.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 08:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: order form redlines + evidence matrix and timeline

David / Monica — this looks good. A couple of clarifying questions from our legal team:

- Can Redwood confirm that snapshot hashes will be verifiable by a third-party auditor (we may need a short verification procedure)?
- For the witness recording, will Redwood redact internal operational logs that contain PII or unrelated customer metadata prior to delivery?

If you can confirm both, we are ready to move toward signature. We’d like the witness test the week of May 3.

Thanks,
Peter

--
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Peter Klein <p.klein@novushealth.ai>, Monica Ruiz <monica.ruiz@novushealth.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy: order form redlines + evidence matrix and timeline

Peter — quick answers:

1) Snapshot verification: yes. We will provide a signed SHA-256 hash and a short verification doc that describes how a third-party auditor can validate the hash against the snapshot artifact. We can include contact details for an ops reviewer to coordinate validation during a defined audit window.

2) Redaction: yes. Witness recordings and any logs we produce will be sanitized for PII and cross-customer metadata before delivery; we will provide a redaction checklist as part of the evidence bundle.

Next steps: Lauren will upload tracked changes to the MSA addendum today, Naomi will upload the finalized EvidenceMatrix (v3) and we’ll schedule a witness session for May 4 (target) pending your signature by EOD May 1. I’ll also open a short commercial note for the optional key-escrow pathway and loop in PM if Novus wants pricing.

David Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai
